text:
For a **weekend tent-camping kit for phones, lights, and camera gear**, I’d pick the **[BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100W solar panel kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2-100w-solar-kit)**. It has a 288Wh battery and a 600W inverter, and the guide estimates about four hours of good sun to refill it. That’s a useful balance for basic campsite electronics without jumping to a much larger setup. The listed price was about $490, though prices can change. ([Dealectric’s camping-kit guide](https://dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-for-tent-camping))

**Caveat:** 288Wh is limited—think charging devices and running lights, not electric cooking or heating. If you’re **car camping** and want substantially more reserve, the **[Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with a 200W panel](https://www.newworldsurvival.com/reviews/solar-generator-kit.html)** offers 1,070Wh, but the power station alone weighs about 24 lb. ([New World Survival’s comparison](https://www.newworldsurvival.com/reviews/solar-generator-kit.html))

judge.top_pick: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W Solar Panel Kit
